    11	/-!
    12	# Widened effectivity for fibrewise-regular sections
    13	
    14	This module is the R2 bridge used by admissible Abel coverage.  A section of a cocycle datum
    15	first cuts intrinsic local equations.  Fibrewise regularity is transported through the section
    16	ring of an arbitrary affine open; the resulting local-equation system is then certified using
    17	away-local arbitrary `AffCoverData` adaptations.  No widened cover piece is identified with one
    18	of the two auxiliary charts used to present the cocycle.
    19	-/
    20	
    21	set_option autoImplicit false
    22	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    23	
    24	universe u
    25	
    26	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
    27	  TopologicalSpace Opposite
    28	open scoped TensorProduct
    29	
    30	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    31	
    32	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    33	
    34	namespace BasicOpenCocycleDatum
    35	
    36	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    37	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    38	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    39	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
    40	variable (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
    41	variable (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤))
    42	
    43	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [IsNoetherianRing B] in
    44	/-- Multiplication-injectivity on a residue fibre is the pure-tensor nonzerodivisor
    45	condition for a component of a cocycle-datum section. -/
    46	theorem component_tmul_one_mem_nonZeroDivisors
    47	    (hfib : ∀ (j : D.index) (p : PrimeSpectrum B), Function.Injective
    48	      ((Scheme.mulSectionEnd B (D.component s j)).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField))
    49	    (j : D.index) (p : PrimeSpectrum B) :
    50	    letI : Algebra B Γ(relCurve C B, D.pieces j) :=
    51	      ((relCurve C B).overAlgebraMap B (D.pieces j)).toAlgebra
    52	    (D.component s j ⊗ₜ[B] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
    53	      Γ(relCurve C B, D.pieces j) ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ∈
    54	        nonZeroDivisors
    55	          (Γ(relCurve C B, D.pieces j) ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
    56	  letI : Algebra B Γ(relCurve C B, D.pieces j) :=
    57	    ((relCurve C B).overAlgebraMap B (D.pieces j)).toAlgebra
    58	  have hend : Scheme.mulSectionEnd B (D.component s j) =
    59	      LinearMap.mulLeft B (D.component s j) := by
    60	    ext t
    61	    simp [Scheme.mulSectionEnd_apply]
    62	  have hinj := hfib j p
    63	  rw [hend, rTensor_mulLeft_eq_mulLeft_tmul p.asIdeal.ResidueField
    64	    (D.component s j)] at hinj
    65	  rw [mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff]
    66	  constructor
    67	  · intro z hz
    68	    apply hinj
    69	    rw [LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, mul_zero]
    70	    exact hz
    71	  · intro z hz
    72	    apply hinj
    73	    rw [LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, mul_zero, mul_comm]
    74	    exact hz
    75	
    76	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] in
    77	/-- A fibrewise-regular component remains a nonzerodivisor after arbitrary coefficient
    78	extension, read through the section ring of its affine open. -/
    79	theorem component_relAffSectionsMap_mem_nonZeroDivisors
    80	    (hfib : ∀ (j : D.index) (p : PrimeSpectrum B), Function.Injective
    81	      ((Scheme.mulSectionEnd B (D.component s j)).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField))
    82	    (B' : Type u) [CommRing B'] [Algebra k B'] [Algebra B B']
    83	    [IsScalarTower k B B'] (j : D.index) :
    84	    relAffSectionsMap C B' (D.pieces j) (D.component s j) ∈
    85	      nonZeroDivisors Γ(relCurve C B', relCurveMap C B B' ⁻¹ᵁ D.pieces j) := by
    86	  letI : Algebra B Γ(relCurve C B, D.pieces j) :=
    87	    ((relCurve C B).overAlgebraMap B (D.pieces j)).toAlgebra
    88	  letI : Module.Flat B Γ(relCurve C B, D.pieces j) :=
    89	    flat_sections_isAffineOpen C B (D.isAffineOpen_pieces j)
    90	  have hbase :=
    91	    Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_forall_tmul_residueField
    92	      (fun p => D.component_tmul_one_mem_nonZeroDivisors s hfib j p) B'
    93	  have hpulled := map_mem_nonZeroDivisors'
    94	    (relSectionsBaseChangeAff C B' (D.isAffineOpen_pieces j)).toRingEquiv hbase
    95	  have hmap : (relSectionsBaseChangeAff C B' (D.isAffineOpen_pieces j)).toRingEquiv
    96	      (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (D.component s j)) =
    97	        relAffSectionsMap C B' (D.pieces j) (D.component s j) := by
    98	    rw [Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight_apply]
    99	    exact relSectionsBaseChangeAff_one_tmul C B'
   100	      (D.isAffineOpen_pieces j) (D.component s j)
   101	  rwa [hmap] at hpulled
   102	
   103	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] in
   104	/-- The pullback of the section-cut equation is the arbitrary-affine section comparison of
   105	the selected component. -/
   106	theorem pullbackEqn_sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular
   107	    (hfib : ∀ (j : D.index) (p : PrimeSpectrum B), Function.Injective
   108	      ((Scheme.mulSectionEnd B (D.component s j)).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField))
   109	    (B' : Type u) [CommRing B'] [Algebra k B'] [Algebra B B']
   110	    [IsScalarTower k B B'] (z : relCurve C B') :
   111	    Scheme.LocalEquations.pullbackEqn (relCurveMap C B B')
   112	        (D.sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular s hfib) z =
   113	      relAffSectionsMap C B'
   114	        (D.pieces (D.pieceIndex ((relCurveMap C B B').base z)))
   115	        (D.component s (D.pieceIndex ((relCurveMap C B B').base z))) := by
   116	  simp [Scheme.LocalEquations.pullbackEqn,
   117	    BasicOpenCocycleDatum.sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular,
   118	    BasicOpenCocycleDatum.sectionLocalEquations,
   119	    relAffSectionsMap, Scheme.resHom]
   120	
   121	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] in
   122	/-- The intrinsic local-equation system cut by a fibrewise-regular section has regular
   123	own-member equations after every field-valued coefficient extension. -/
   124	theorem germ_self_pullbackEqn_sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular
   125	    (hfib : ∀ (j : D.index) (p : PrimeSpectrum B), Function.Injective
   126	      ((Scheme.mulSectionEnd B (D.component s j)).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField))
   127	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra B L]
   128	    [IsScalarTower k B L] (z : relCurve C L) :
   129	    ((relCurve C L).presheaf.germ
   130	      (((D.sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular s hfib).cover.pullback
   131	        (relCurveMap C B L)).opens z) z
   132	      (((D.sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular s hfib).cover.pullback
   133	        (relCurveMap C B L)).mem_opens z)).hom
   134	      (Scheme.LocalEquations.pullbackEqn (relCurveMap C B L)
   135	        (D.sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular s hfib) z) ∈
   136	      nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C L).presheaf.stalk z) := by
   137	  let j := D.pieceIndex ((relCurveMap C B L).base z)
   138	  have hsec := D.component_relAffSectionsMap_mem_nonZeroDivisors s hfib L j
   139	  have hopen : IsAffineOpen (relCurveMap C B L ⁻¹ᵁ D.pieces j) :=
   140	    isAffineOpen_relCurveMap_preimage C L (D.isAffineOpen_pieces j)
   141	  have hz : z ∈ relCurveMap C B L ⁻¹ᵁ D.pieces j :=
   142	    D.mem_pieces_pieceIndex ((relCurveMap C B L).base z)
   143	  have hgerm := hopen.germ_mem_nonZeroDivisors hsec (y := z) hz
   144	  rw [D.pullbackEqn_sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular s hfib L z]
   145	  dsimp only [j] at hgerm
   146	  simpa only [BasicOpenCocycleDatum.sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular,
   147	    BasicOpenCocycleDatum.sectionLocalEquations,
   148	    Scheme.PointedCover.pullback_opens,
   149	    BasicOpenCocycleDatum.pointedCover_opens] using hgerm
   150	
   151	end BasicOpenCocycleDatum
   152	
   153	section WidenedEffectivity
   154	
   155	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   156	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   157	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   158	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
   159	variable (n : ℕ)
   160	variable (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations)
   161	
   162	noncomputable local instance instIsIntegralRelCurveEffectivity
   163	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] : IsIntegral (relCurve C L) :=
   164	  instIsIntegralBaseChange C L
   165	
   166	noncomputable local instance instSmoothRelCurveEffectivity
   167	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
   168	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (.of L)) :=
   169	  instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C L
   170	
   171	noncomputable local instance instQuasiCompactRelCurveEffectivity
   172	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
   173	    QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (.of L)) :=
   174	  instQuasiCompactBaseChange C L
   175	
   176	noncomputable local instance instFiniteH0RelCurveEffectivity
   177	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
   178	    Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0) :=
   179	  instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C L
   180	
   181	noncomputable local instance instFiniteH1RelCurveEffectivity
   182	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
   183	    Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1) :=
   184	  instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C L
   185	
   186	set_option maxHeartbeats 8000000 in
   187	-- The certified-adaptation assembly elaborates dependent pulled equations at two field levels.
   188	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 800000 in
   189	/-- A fibrewise-regular local-equation system of constant fibre class degree `n` has an
   190	away-local widened certificate at every prime of its Noetherian base. -/
   191	theorem exists_away_certifiedAff_of_fibrewiseRegular_of_classDeg
   192	    (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
   193	    (hreg : ∀ (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra R L]
   194	      [IsScalarTower k R L], ∀ z : relCurve C L,
   195	      ((relCurve C L).presheaf.germ
   196	        ((d.cover.pullback (relCurveMap C R L)).opens z) z
   197	        ((d.cover.pullback (relCurveMap C R L)).mem_opens z)).hom
   198	        (Scheme.LocalEquations.pullbackEqn (relCurveMap C R L) d z) ∈
   199	          nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C L).presheaf.stalk z))
   200	    (hdeg : ∀ (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra R L]
   201	      [IsScalarTower k R L],
   202	      classDeg L (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C R L) d.picClass) = (n : ℤ))
   203	    (p : PrimeSpectrum R) :
   204	    ∃ r, r ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
   205	      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) :=
   206	        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away r) r
   207	      ∃ (Dr : AffCoverData C (Localization.Away r))
   208	        (A : AffAdaptation Dr
   209	          (d.pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r))
   210	            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
   211	              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) d))),
   212	        A.IsCertified n := by
   213	  have hfinite :=
   214	    Scheme.LocalEquations.fibre_supportLocus_finite_of_forall_self_aff
   215	      C R d p (fun z => hreg p.asIdeal.ResidueField z)
   216	  obtain ⟨r, hr, Dr, A, hsw⟩ :=
   217	    Scheme.LocalEquations.exists_away_affAdaptation_swallowedBy_of_finite_fibre
   218	      C R pi d p hfinite
   219	  letI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) :=
   220	    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away r) r
   221	  refine ⟨r, hr, Dr, A, ?_⟩
   222	  obtain ⟨j0, hsub, hmiss⟩ := hsw
   223	  have hfin : ∀ j, Module.Finite (Localization.Away r) (A.colength j) :=
   224	    A.forall_finite_colength_of_swallowedBy ⟨j0, hsub, hmiss⟩
   225	  have hproj : ∀ j, Module.Projective (Localization.Away r) (A.colength j) := fun j => by
   226	    haveI := hfin j
   227	    exact A.projective_colength_of_forall_tmul_residueField j fun q =>
   228	      A.eqn_tmul_one_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_self_pullbackEqn j q fun z => by
   229	        have hcomp : relCurveMap C (Localization.Away r) q.asIdeal.ResidueField
   230	              ≫ relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r) =
   231	            relCurveMap C R q.asIdeal.ResidueField :=
   232	          relCurveMap_comp (R' := Localization.Away r)
   233	            (R'' := q.asIdeal.ResidueField)
   234	        have heq := Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_comp hcomp d
   235	          (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
   236	            (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) d) z
   237	        exact heq ▸ hreg q.asIdeal.ResidueField z
   238	  exact A.isCertified_of_swallowedBy_of_c1_of_rank_piece hsub hmiss hfin hproj fun q =>
   239	    A.rankAtStalk_colength_eq_of_swallowedBy_of_pulled_degree
   240	      j0 hsub hmiss hfin hproj q (by
   241	        rw [← classDeg_picClass,
   242	          Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_presentationDivisor,
   243	          Scheme.LocalEquations.presentation_picClass,
   244	          A.picClass_pulledEquations q.asIdeal.ResidueField hproj,
   245	          Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass_pullback,
   246	          ← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp,
   247	          relCurveMap_comp (R' := Localization.Away r)
   248	            (R'' := q.asIdeal.ResidueField)]
   249	        exact hdeg q.asIdeal.ResidueField)
   250	
   251	set_option maxHeartbeats 8000000 in
   252	-- The definition elaborates the full dependent certificate family produced above.
   253	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 800000 in
   254	/-- The widened divisor class represented by a fibrewise-regular, constant-degree intrinsic
   255	local-equation system. -/
   256	noncomputable def divFamZarAffOfFibrewiseRegularLocalEquations
   257	    (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
   258	    (hreg : ∀ (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra R L]
   259	      [IsScalarTower k R L], ∀ z : relCurve C L,
   260	      ((relCurve C L).presheaf.germ
   261	        ((d.cover.pullback (relCurveMap C R L)).opens z) z
   262	        ((d.cover.pullback (relCurveMap C R L)).mem_opens z)).hom
   263	        (Scheme.LocalEquations.pullbackEqn (relCurveMap C R L) d z) ∈
   264	          nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C L).presheaf.stalk z))
   265	    (hdeg : ∀ (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra R L]
   266	      [IsScalarTower k R L],
   267	      classDeg L (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C R L) d.picClass) = (n : ℤ)) :
   268	    DivFamZarAff C R n :=
   269	  divFamZarAff_of_forall_prime_certified_adaptation
   270	    (exists_away_certifiedAff_of_fibrewiseRegular_of_classDeg C n d pi hreg hdeg)
   271	
   272	@[simp]
   273	theorem picClass_divFamZarAffOfFibrewiseRegularLocalEquations
   274	    (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
   275	    (hreg : ∀ (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra R L]
   276	      [IsScalarTower k R L], ∀ z : relCurve C L,
   277	      ((relCurve C L).presheaf.germ
   278	        ((d.cover.pullback (relCurveMap C R L)).opens z) z
   279	        ((d.cover.pullback (relCurveMap C R L)).mem_opens z)).hom
   280	        (Scheme.LocalEquations.pullbackEqn (relCurveMap C R L) d z) ∈
   281	          nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C L).presheaf.stalk z))
   282	    (hdeg : ∀ (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra R L]
   283	      [IsScalarTower k R L],
   284	      classDeg L (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C R L) d.picClass) = (n : ℤ)) :
   285	    DivFamZarAff.picClass
   286	      (divFamZarAffOfFibrewiseRegularLocalEquations C n d pi hreg hdeg) = d.picClass :=
   287	  rfl
   288	
   289	end WidenedEffectivity
   290	
   291	end AlgebraicGeometry

    18	namespace AlgebraicGeometry

    20	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    21	
    22	namespace BasicOpenCoverData
    23	
    24	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    25	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
    26	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
    27	
    28	/-- The pinned-chart side containing a basic-open piece. -/
    29	def pinnedSide (D : BasicOpenCoverData C B pi) : D.index → Bool
    30	  | Sum.inl _ => false
    31	  | Sum.inr _ => true
    32	
    33	/-- The pinned-chart section cutting out a basic-open piece. -/
    34	noncomputable def pinnedGenerator (D : BasicOpenCoverData C B pi) :
    35	    (j : D.index) → Γ(relCurve C B, relPinnedChart C B pi (D.pinnedSide j))
    36	  | Sum.inl j => D.h₀ j
    37	  | Sum.inr j => D.h₁ j
    38	
    39	theorem pieces_eq_basicOpen_pinnedGenerator
    40	    (D : BasicOpenCoverData C B pi) (j : D.index) :
    41	    D.pieces j = (relCurve C B).basicOpen (D.pinnedGenerator j) := by
    42	  cases j <;> rfl
    43	
    44	end BasicOpenCoverData

    46	namespace BasicOpenCocycleDatum
    47	
    48	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    49	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
    50	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
    51	
    52	/-- A datum component, with its open written using the uniform pinned generator. -/
    53	noncomputable def pinnedComponent (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
    54	    (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤)) :
    55	    (j : D.index) → Γ(relCurve C B,
    56	      (relCurve C B).basicOpen (D.toBasicOpenCoverData.pinnedGenerator j))
    57	  | Sum.inl j => D.component s (Sum.inl j)
    58	  | Sum.inr j => D.component s (Sum.inr j)
    59	
    60	/-- Fibrewise injectivity of multiplication by a datum component gives the ring-theoretic
    61	nonzerodivisor condition on its pure tensor. -/
    62	theorem component_tmul_one_mem_nonZeroDivisors
    63	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
    64	    (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤))
    65	    (hfib : ∀ (j : D.index) (p : PrimeSpectrum B), Function.Injective
    66	      ((Scheme.mulSectionEnd B (D.component s j)).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField))
    67	    (j : D.index) (p : PrimeSpectrum B) :
    68	    letI : Algebra B Γ(relCurve C B, D.pieces j) :=
    69	      ((relCurve C B).overAlgebraMap B (D.pieces j)).toAlgebra
    70	    (D.component s j ⊗ₜ[B] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
    71	      Γ(relCurve C B, D.pieces j) ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ∈
    72	        nonZeroDivisors
    73	          (Γ(relCurve C B, D.pieces j) ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
    74	  letI : Algebra B Γ(relCurve C B, D.pieces j) :=
    75	    ((relCurve C B).overAlgebraMap B (D.pieces j)).toAlgebra
    76	  have hend : Scheme.mulSectionEnd B (D.component s j) =
    77	      LinearMap.mulLeft B (D.component s j) := by
    78	    ext t
    79	    simp [Scheme.mulSectionEnd_apply]
    80	  have hinj := hfib j p
    81	  rw [hend, rTensor_mulLeft_eq_mulLeft_tmul p.asIdeal.ResidueField
    82	    (D.component s j)] at hinj
    83	  rw [mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff]
    84	  constructor
    85	  · intro z hz
    86	    apply hinj
    87	    rw [LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, mul_zero]
    88	    exact hz
    89	  · intro z hz
    90	    apply hinj
    91	    rw [LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, mul_zero, mul_comm]
    92	    exact hz
    93	
    94	/-- Fibrewise-regular datum components remain nonzerodivisors on their pinned basic opens
    95	after every coefficient-ring extension. -/
    96	theorem pinnedComponent_baseChange_mem_nonZeroDivisors [IsNoetherianRing B]
    97	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
    98	    (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤))

    13	local lifts into local surjectivity on the big etale site. It also packages the passage from

    15	one of its etale presentations.

    18	or quotient assertion.

    33	/-- A sieve on a scheme is etale-covering if its pullback to every member of the canonical
    34	affine open cover is etale-covering. -/
    35	theorem mem_etaleTopology_of_pullback_affine {T : Scheme.{u}} (S : Sieve T)
    36	    (h : ∀ (j : T.affineCover.I₀), S.pullback (T.affineCover.f j) ∈
    37	      Scheme.etaleTopology (T.affineCover.X j)) :
    38	    S ∈ Scheme.etaleTopology T := by
    39	  have hcov : (Sieve.generate (Presieve.ofArrows T.affineCover.X T.affineCover.f))
    40	      ∈ Scheme.etaleTopology T := by
    41	    apply Scheme.zariskiTopology_le_etaleTopology
    42	    exact Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mpr
    43	      ⟨T.affineCover, Sieve.le_generate _⟩
    44	  refine Scheme.etaleTopology.transitive hcov S ?_
    45	  rintro Y g ⟨V, a, b, ⟨j⟩, rfl⟩
    46	  rw [Sieve.pullback_comp]
    47	  exact Scheme.etaleTopology.pullback_stable a (h j)
    48	
    49	/-- To prove local surjectivity on the big etale site, it suffices to produce an etale cover
    50	with local lifts over every affine test scheme. -/
    51	theorem isLocallySurjective_etale_of_affine
    52	    {F G : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : F ⟶ G)
    53	    (h : ∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine Y] (s : G.obj (op Y)),
    54	      ∃ (cover : Y.Cover.{u} (Scheme.precoverage @Etale)),
    55	        ∀ j : cover.I₀, ∃ x : F.obj (op (cover.X j)),
    56	          f.app (op (cover.X j)) x = G.map (cover.f j).op s) :
    57	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.etaleTopology f where
    58	  imageSieve_mem {U} s := by
    59	    apply mem_etaleTopology_of_pullback_affine
    60	    intro j
    61	    rw [Presheaf.pullback_imageSieve]
    62	    obtain ⟨cover, hcover⟩ :=
    63	      h (U.affineCover.X j) (G.map (U.affineCover.f j).op s)
    64	    refine (Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff (P := @Etale)).mpr ⟨cover, ?_⟩
    65	    rintro Y g ⟨i⟩
    66	    exact hcover i

    70	/-- The spectrum of the carrier of an algebraic etale cover is a singleton etale cover of
    71	the spectrum of the base algebra. -/
    72	noncomputable def etaleSchemeCover {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    73	    (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) :
    74	    (Spec (.of A)).Cover (Scheme.precoverage @Etale) :=
    75	  Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers PUnit (fun _ => Spec (.of E.Carrier))
    76	    (fun _ => Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A E.Carrier)))
    77	    (fun x => by
    78	      obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := E.comap_surjective x
    79	      exact ⟨PUnit.unit, y, hy⟩)
    80	    (fun _ => by
    81	      rw [HasRingHomProperty.Spec_iff (P := @Etale)]
    82	      exact RingHom.etale_algebraMap.mpr inferInstance)

    88	/-- `mapAlg` agrees with the instance-based affine restriction map when the underlying ring
    89	homomorphism is the chosen `A`-algebra structure on `B`. -/
    90	theorem mapAlg_eq_map_of_toRingHom_eq_algebraMap
    91	    {k A B : Type u} [Field k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [CommRing B]
    92	    [Algebra k B] [Algebra A B] [IsScalarTower k A B]
    93	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (phi : A →ₐ[k] B)
    94	    (hphi : phi.toRingHom = algebraMap A B) (a : PicEtAff C A) :
    95	    PicEtAff.mapAlg C phi a = PicEtAff.map C B a := by
    96	  have hAlg : phi.toRingHom.toAlgebra = (inferInstance : Algebra A B) :=
    97	    Algebra.algebra_ext _ _ fun r => by
    98	      change phi r = algebraMap A B r
    99	      exact DFunLike.congr_fun hphi r
   100	  unfold PicEtAff.mapAlg
   101	  subst hAlg
   102	  rfl
   103	
   104	/-- Restricting an affine PicEt presentation along the map to its own cover carrier produces
   105	the honest class represented by its descent datum. -/
   106	theorem mapAlg_mk_eq_unit_self
   107	    {k A : Type u} [Field k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   108	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   109	    (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (x : descentClasses C E) :
   110	    PicEtAff.mapAlg C ((Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k)
   111	        (PicEtAff.mk C E x)
   112	      = PicEtAff.unit C E.Carrier
   113	          (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) := by
   114	  rw [mapAlg_eq_map_of_toRingHom_eq_algebraMap C _ rfl]
   115	  exact PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_self C E x

     8	/-!
     9	# Application formulas for the admissible widened Abel map
    10	
    11	This file isolates the map-level equalities needed after a widened divisor family has been
    12	constructed on an affine test. It exposes the chart datum chosen inside the admissible map,
    13	computes a represented point under the Sigma-extended Abel transformation, identifies the
    14	affine Abel value after the vehicle collapse, and packages the final cancellation of the
    15	fixed chart twists.
    16	
    17	No quotient, atlas, or representability conclusion is asserted here.
    18	-/
    19	
    20	set_option autoImplicit false
    21	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    22	
    23	universe u
    24	
    25	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory Opposite
    26	
    27	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    28	
    29	attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    30	
    31	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    32	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    33	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    34	
    35	noncomputable section
    36	
    37	variable (C) in
    38	/-- The chart index and divisor chosen inside the admissible Abel map can be exposed without
    39	choosing new data. The equality is definitional after unfolding the admissible map. -/
    40	theorem exists_abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible_eq :
    41	    ∃ (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    42	      (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
    43	        = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C)
    44	          - (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C : ℤ)),
    45	      abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible C =
    46	        abelSigmaChartAff C (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C)
    47	          (divFunctorAff_admissible_representableBy C) m Z hdeg := by
    48	  dsimp only [abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible]
    49	  exact ⟨_, _, _, rfl⟩
    50	
    51	variable {n : ℕ}
    52	
    53	/-- Classifying a section with a representer and then evaluating the Sigma-extended Abel map
    54	at the underlying scheme morphism returns the original section's chart value. The equality of
    55	the two structure morphisms is handled by sigma-extension extensionality. -/
    56	theorem abelSigmaChartAff_app_homEquiv_symm
    57	    {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    58	    (rep : (divFunctorAff C n).RepresentableBy D)
    59	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    60	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
    61	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
    62	    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (a : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    63	    (s : divFamZarAff C n (Over.mk a)) :
    64	    let q := rep.homEquiv.symm s
    65	    (abelSigmaChartAff C n rep m Z hdeg).app (op Y) q.left =
    66	      (⟨a, (chartValueAffTrans C n m Z hdeg).app (op (Over.mk a)) s⟩ :
    67	        (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y)) := by
    68	  let q := rep.homEquiv.symm s
    69	  change (abelSigmaChartAff C n rep m Z hdeg).app (op Y) q.left =
    70	    (⟨a, (chartValueAffTrans C n m Z hdeg).app (op (Over.mk a)) s⟩ :
    71	      (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y))
    72	  change (⟨q.left ≫ D.hom, _⟩ :
    73	      (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y)) =
    74	    ⟨a, (chartValueAffTrans C n m Z hdeg).app (op (Over.mk a)) s⟩
    75	  refine Over.sigmaExtension_ext (pic0TypeFunctor C) q.w ?_
    76	  let e := Over.mkCongr q.w
    77	  let q' : Over.mk (q.left ≫ D.hom) ⟶ D :=
    78	    Over.homMk (U := Over.mk (q.left ≫ D.hom)) q.left
    79	  change (pic0TypeFunctor C).map e.op
    80	      ((chartValueAffTrans C n m Z hdeg).app (op (Over.mk a)) s) =
    81	    (chartValueAffTrans C n m Z hdeg).app
    82	      (op (Over.mk (q.left ≫ D.hom))) (rep.homEquiv q')
    83	  have hhom : e ≫ q = q' := by
    84	    apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
    85	    exact Category.id_comp _
    86	  have hq : rep.homEquiv q = s := by
    87	    dsimp only [q]
    88	    exact Equiv.apply_symm_apply rep.homEquiv s
    89	  have hfamily : rep.homEquiv q' =
    90	      (divFunctorAff C n).map e.op s := by
    91	    calc
    92	      rep.homEquiv q' = rep.homEquiv (e ≫ q) := congrArg rep.homEquiv hhom.symm
    93	      _ = (divFunctorAff C n).map e.op (rep.homEquiv q) := rep.homEquiv_comp e q
    94	      _ = (divFunctorAff C n).map e.op s := congrArg _ hq
    95	  have hnat := ConcreteCategory.congr_hom
    96	    ((chartValueAffTrans C n m Z hdeg).naturality e.op) s
    97	  calc
    98	    _ = (chartValueAffTrans C n m Z hdeg).app
    99	        (op (Over.mk (q.left ≫ D.hom))) ((divFunctorAff C n).map e.op s) := by
   100	      simpa only [ConcreteCategory.comp_apply] using hnat.symm
   101	    _ = _ := congrArg _ hfamily.symm
   102	
   103	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] in
   104	/-- On an affine test, passing a widened affine family through the inverse vehicle comparison
   105	and then taking its Abel value recovers the direct affine Abel value. -/
   106	theorem picEtAffineEquiv_abelDivAff'_affineEquiv_symm
   107	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] (F : DivFamZarAff C A n) :
   108	    picEtAffineEquiv C A
   109	        (abelDivAff' C n (overSpec k A) ((divFamZarAffAffineEquiv C n A).symm F))
   110	      = abelDivAffPlus C A F := by
   111	  rw [picEtAffineEquiv_abelDivAff', Equiv.apply_symm_apply]
   112	
   113	/-- If the Abel value of a widened family is the inverse chart twist of a target degree-zero
   114	class, then the chart transformation sends that family to the target itself. -/
   115	theorem chartValueAffTrans_app_eq_of_abelDivAff'_eq_chartTwist
   116	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   117	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
   118	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
   119	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (s : divFamZarAff C n T)
   120	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T)
   121	    (habel : abelDivAff' C n T s = chartTwist C m Z T lam.1) :
   122	    (chartValueAffTrans C n m Z hdeg).app (op T) s = lam := by
   123	  apply Subtype.ext
   124	  rw [chartValueAffTrans_app_coe]
   125	  change chartValueAff C n m Z T s = lam.1
   126	  rw [chartValueAff, habel, chartTwist]
   127	  group
   128	
   129	end

/bin/bash -lc "lake env lean /dev/stdin <<'EOF'
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicRepDatum
set_option autoImplicit false
universe u
open CategoryTheory
open AlgebraicGeometry
abbrev AbelEndpoint {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) :=
  Sigma fun Q : Over (Spec (.of k)) => (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy Q
example {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
    AbelEndpoint C → Nonempty (AbelEndpoint C) := fun h => ⟨h⟩
noncomputable example {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
    Nonempty (AbelEndpoint C) → AbelEndpoint C := Classical.choice
example {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
    AbelEndpoint C → ∃ Q : Over (Spec (.of k)), Nonempty ((pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy Q) :=
  fun h => ⟨h.1, ⟨h.2⟩⟩
noncomputable example {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
    (∃ Q : Over (Spec (.of k)), Nonempty ((pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy Q)) → AbelEndpoint C := by
  rintro ⟨Q, h⟩
  exact ⟨Q, Classical.choice h⟩

  1266	\section{The several Picard functors}\label{sc:Pfctrs}
  1267	\renewcommand{\theequation}{\thethm.\arabic{equation}}
  1268	Our first job is to identify a likely candidate for the functor of
  1269	points of the Picard scheme.  In fact, there are several reasonable such
  1270	Picard functors, and each one is more likely to be representable than
  1271	the preceding.  In this section, they all are formally introduced and
  1272	compared.
  1273	
  1274	\begin{dfn}\label{df:aPf}
  1275	 The {\it absolute Picard functor} $\Pic_X$ is the functor from  the
  1276	 category of (locally Noetherian) $S$-schemes $T$ to the category of
  1277	abelian groups defined by the formula
  1278		$$\Pic_X(T):=\Pic(X_T).$$
  1279	\end{dfn}
  1280	
  1281	The absolute Picard functor  is a ``prepared presheaf'' in this
  1282	sense: given any family of  $S$-schemes $T_i$, we have
  1283		$$\Pic_X\bigl(\textstyle\coprod T_i\bigr)=\prod\Pic_X(T_i).$$
  1284	 Hence, given a covering family $\{T_i\to T\}$ in the Zariski topology,
  1285	the \'etale topology, or any other Grothendieck topology on the category
  1286	of $S$-schemes, there is no harm, when we consider the sheaf associated
  1287	to $\Pic_X$, in working simply with the single map $T'\to T$ where
  1288	$T':=\coprod T_i$.  And doing so lightens the notation, making for
  1289	easier reading. Therefore, we do so throughout, calling $T'\to T$ simply
  1290	a {\it covering\/} in the given topology.
  1291	
  1292	The absolute Picard functor $\Pic_X$ is never a separated presheaf in
  1293	the Zariski topology.  Indeed, take an $S$-scheme $T$ that carries an
  1294	invertible sheaf $\mc N$ such that $f^*_T\mc N$ is nontrivial.  (For
  1295	example, take $T:=\I P^1_X$ and $\mc N:=\mc O_{\!T}(1)$.  Then the diagonal
  1296	map $X\to X\x X$ induces a section $g$ of $f_T$; that is, $gf_T=1_T$.
  1297	Hence $f^*_T\mc N$ is nontrivial.)  Now, there exists a Zariski covering
  1298	$T'\to T$ such that the pullback $\mc N|T'$ is trivial; here, $T'$ is
  1299	simply the disjoint union of the subsets in a suitable ordinary open
  1300	covering of $T$.  So the pullback $f^*_{T'}\mc N|X_{T'}$ is trivial too.
  1301	Thus $\Pic_X(T)$ has a nonzero element whose restriction is zero in

  1303	
  1304	According to descent theory, every representable functor is a sheaf in

  2128	on the fibers of $X/S$.  A class is, by definition, represented by an
  2129	$\mc L$ on an $X_k$ where $k$ is a field containing the residue field
  2130	$k_s$ of a (scheme) point $s\in S$; an $\mc L'$ on an $X_{k'}$
  2131	represents the same class if and only if there is a third field $k''$
  2132	containing the other two such that $\mc L|X_{k''}\simeq\mc L'|X_{k''}$.
  2133	 \end{ex}

  2135	\begin{dfn}\label{dfn:Abel}
  2136	 The {\it Abel map\/} is the natural map of functors
  2137		$$A_{X/S}(T)\:\Div_{X/S}(T)\to \Pic_{X/S}(T)$$
  2138	 defined by sending a relative effective divisor $D$ on $X_T/T$ to the
  2139	sheaf $\mc O_{\!X_T}(D)$.  The target $\Pic_{X/S}$ may be replaced by any
  2140	of its associated sheaves.  %% And, of course,
  2141	 If $\IPic_{X/S}$ exists,
  2142	then the term {\it Abel map\/} may refer to the corresponding map of
  2143	schemes
  2144		$$\I A_{X/S}\:\IDiv_{X/S}\to\IPic_{X/S}.$$
  2145	 \end{dfn}
  2146	
  2147	\begin{ex}\label{ex:PQ-Abel}
  2148	  Assume $X/S$ is proper and flat with integral geometric fibers. Assume
  2149	$\IPic_{X/S}$ exists, and denote it by $P$.  View $\IDiv_{X/S}$ as a
  2150	$P$-scheme via the Abel map.  Assume a universal sheaf $\mc P$ exists,
  2151	and let $\mc Q$ be the sheaf on $P$ associated to $\mc P$ as in
  2152	Subsection~\ref{sb:Q}.  Show $\I P(\mc Q)=\IDiv_{X/S}$ as $P$-schemes.
  2153	 \end{ex}

  2155	\begin{thm}[Main]\label{th:main}
  2156	 Assume $f\:X\to S$ is projective Zariski locally over $S$, and is flat
  2157	with integral geometric fibers.
  2158	
  2159	\tu{(1)} Then $\IPic_{X/S}$ exists, is separated and locally of finite
  2160	type over $S$, and represents $\Pic_{(X/S)\et}$.
  2161	
  2162	\tu{(2)} If also $S$ is Noetherian and $X/S$ is projective, then
  2163	$\IPic_{X/S}$ is a disjoint union of open
  2164	 subschemes, each an increasing union of open quasi-projective
  2165	$S$-schemes.
  2166	 \end{thm}
  2167	
  2168	\begin{proof}
  2169	 By~\cite[(0, 4.5.5), p.~106]{EGAG}, it is a local matter on $S$ to
  2170	represent a Zariski sheaf on the category of $S$-schemes.  Moreover, it
  2171	is also a local matter on $S$ to prove that an $S$-scheme is separated
  2172	and locally of finite type.  Hence, in order to prove (1), we may assume
  2173	$S$ is Noetherian and $X/S$ is projective.
  2174	
  2175	Plainly an $S$-scheme is separated if it is a disjoint union of
  2176	separated open subschemes, or if it is an increasing union of
  2177	separated open subschemes.  Hence (1) follows from (2).
  2178	
  2179	To prove (2), owing to Yoneda's lemma, we may view the category of
  2180	schemes as a full subcategory of the category of functors by identifying
  2181	a scheme $T$ with its functor of points.  Denote this functor too by $T$
  2182	in order to lighten the notation. And say that the functor is a scheme,
  2183	as well as that it is representable.  Also, set
  2184	 $$P:=\Pic_{(X/S)\et}.$$
  2185	  Note $P(T)= \Hom(T,P)$. %% \{\,T\to P\,\}$.
  2186	
  2187	Given a polynomial $\phi\in\bb Q[n]$, let $P^\phi\subset P$ be the
  2188	\'etale subsheaf associated to the presheaf whose $T$-points are
  2189	represented by the invertible sheaves $\mc L$ on $X_T$ such that we have
  2190	 \begin{equation}\label{eq:phi}
  2191		\chi(X_t,\mc L^{-1}_t(n)) = \phi(n) \text{ for all $t\in T$}.
  2192	 \end{equation}
  2193	 Notice that this presheaf is well defined, because (\ref{eq:phi})
  2194	remains valid after any base change $p\:T'\to T$; indeed, for any $t'\in
  2195	T'$, for any $i$, and for any $n$, we have
  2196		$$\uH^i\bigl(X_{t'},\mc L^{-1}_{t'}(n)\bigr)
  2197	   =\uH^i\bigl(X_{p(t')},\mc L^{-1}_{p(t')}(n)\bigr)\ox_{k_t}k_{t'}$$
  2198	 because cohomology commutes with flat base change by \cite[Prp.~III,
  2199	9.3, p.~255]{Ha83}.  Hence $P^\phi$ is well defined too.
  2200	
  2201	Fix a map $T\to P$, and represent it by means of an \'etale covering
  2202	$p\:T'\to T$ and an invertible sheaf $\mc L'$ on $X_{T'}$.  Consider the
  2203	subset ${T'}^{\phi}\subset T'$ defined as follows:
  2204	       $${T'}^{\phi}:=\{\,t'\in T'\mid
  2205	       \chi\bigl(X_{t'},\mc L^{-1}_{t'}(n)\bigr) = \phi(n)\,\}.$$
  2206	 Then ${T'}^{\phi}$  is  open by \cite[7.9.11]{EGAIII2}.
  2207	
  2208	Set $T^\phi:=p({T'}^{\phi})$.  Then $T^\phi\subset T$ is
  2209	open as ${T'}^{\phi}\subset T'$  is  open and $p$ is  \'etale.
  2210	
  2211	Moreover, ${T'}^{\phi}=p^{-1}(T^\phi)$.  Indeed, let $t'\in
  2212	p^{-1}(T^\phi)$.  Say $p(t')=p(t'_1)$ where $t'_1\in {T'}^\phi$.  Now,
  2213	there is an \'etale covering $T''\to T'\x_TT'$ such that the two
  2214	pullbacks of $\mc L'$ to $X_{T''}$ are isomorphic.  Let $t''\in T''$
  2215	have image $t'\in T'$ under the first map $T''\to T'$ and have the image
  2216	$t'_1\in T'$ under the second map.  Then
  2217		$$\chi\bigl(X_{t'},\mc L^{-1}_{t'}(n)\bigr)
  2218		 = \chi\bigl(X_{t''},\mc L^{-1}_{t''}(n)\bigr)
  2219		 = \chi\bigl(X_{t'_1},\mc L^{-1}_{t'_1}(n)\bigr) = \phi(n).$$
  2220	 Hence $t'\in {T'}^\phi$.  Thus ${T'}^{\phi}\supset
  2221	p^{-1}(T^\phi)$. Therefore, ${T'}^{\phi}=p^{-1}(T^\phi)$.
  2222	
  2223	Furthermore, $T^\phi$ is (represents) the fiber product of functors
  2224	$P^\phi\x_PT$.  Indeed, to see they have the same $R$-points, let
  2225	$r\:R\to T$ be a map; form $R':=R\x_TT'$ and $r'\:R'\to T'$.  Suppose
  2226	$r$ factors through $T^\phi$.  Then $r'$ factors through ${T'}^{\phi}$.
  2227	So $R'\to T'\to P$ factors through $P^\phi$ essentially by definition.
  2228	Now, $R'\to R$ is an \'etale covering.  Hence $R\to T\to P$ factors
  2229	through $P^\phi$ since $P^\phi$ is an \'etale sheaf.
  2230	
  2231	Conversely, suppose $R\to T\to P$ factors through $P^\phi$.  Then $R\to
  2232	P$ is defined by means of an \'etale covering $R''\to R$ and an
  2233	invertible sheaf $\mc L''$ on $X_{R''}$ such that $\chi(X_u,\mc {\mc
  2234	L''}^{-1}_u(n)) = \phi(n)$ for all $u\in R''$.  Since both $\mc L''$ and
  2235	$\mc L'$ define $R\to P$, there is an \'etale covering $R'''\to
  2236	R''\x_RR'$ such that the pullbacks of $\mc L''$ and $\mc L'$ to
  2237	$X_{R'''}$ are isomorphic.  Hence the image of $r'\:R'\to T'$ lies in
  2238	${T'}^{\phi}$.  But the latter is open.  Hence $r'$ factors through it.
  2239	Therefore,   $r\:R\to T$ factors through $T^\phi$.  Thus  $T^\phi$ and
  2240	$P^\phi\x_PT$ have the same $R$-points.
  2241	
  2242	Let $\phi$ vary.  Plainly the ${T'}^{\phi}$ are disjoint and cover $T'$.
  2243	So the ${T}^{\phi}$ are disjoint and cover $T$.  Hence, by a general
  2244	result~\cite[(0, 4.5.4), p.~103]{EGAG}, if the $P^\phi$ are
  2245	(representable by) schemes, then $P$ is their disjoint union.  Thus it
  2246	remains to represent each $P^\phi$ by an increasing union of open
  2247	quasi-projective $S$-schemes.
  2248	
  2249	Fix $\phi$.  Given $m\in \bb Z$, let $P^\phi_m\subset P^\phi$ be the
  2250	\'etale subsheaf associated to the presheaf whose $T$-points are
  2251	represented by the $\mc L$ on $X_T$ such that, in addition to
  2252	(\ref{eq:phi}), we have
  2253	 \begin{equation}\label{eq:4b}
  2254		\tu R^if_{\smash{T}*}\mc L(n)=0
  2255	    \text{ for all }i\ge1\text{ and }n\ge m.
  2256	  \end{equation}
  2257	 Notice that this presheaf is well defined, because (\ref{eq:4b})
  2258	remains valid after any base change $p\:T'\to T$, as is shown next.
  2259	
  2260	First, let's see that (\ref{eq:4b}) is equivalent to the following
  2261	condition:
  2262	 \begin{equation}\label{eq:4c}
  2263		\uH^i(X_t,\mc L_t(n))=0

  2267	$i$, $t$ and $n$, if $\uH^i(X_t,\mc L_t(n))=0$, then $\tu
  2268	R^if_{\smash{T}*}\bigl(\mc L(n)\ox f_T^*\mc N\bigr)_t=0$ for all
  2269	quasi-coherent $\mc N$ on $T$ by \cite[7.5.3]{EGAIII2} or \cite[Cor.~2.1
  2270	p.~68]{OB72}.
  2271	
  2272	Conversely, assume (\ref{eq:4b}).  Fix $t$ and $n$.  Let's proceed by
  2273	descending induction on $i$ to prove $\uH^i(X_t,\mc L_t(n))$ vanishes.
  2274	It vanishes for $i\gg 1$ by Serre's Theorem \cite[2.2.2]{EGAIII1}.
  2275	Suppose it vanishes for some $i\ge2$.  Then $\tu
  2276	R^if_{\smash{T}*}\bigl(\mc L(n)\ox f_T^*\mc N\bigr)_t$ vanishes for all
  2277	quasi-coherent $\mc N$ on $T$, as just noted.  So $\tu
  2278	R^{i-1}f_{\smash{T}*}\bigl(\mc L(n)\ox f_T^*\mc N\bigr)_t$ is right
  2279	exact in $\mc N$ owing to the long exact sequence of higher direct
  2280	images.  Therefore, by general principles, there is a natural
  2281	isomorphism of functors
  2282	 	$$ \tu R^{i-1}f_{\smash{T}*}(\mc L(n))_t\ox \mc N_t\risom
  2283	 	 \tu R^{i-1}f_{\smash{T}*}\bigl(\mc L(n)\ox f_T^*\mc N\bigr)_t.$$
  2284	 Since (\ref{eq:4b}) holds, both source and target vanish.
  2285	Taking $\mc N:=k_t$ yields the vanishing of $\uH^{i-1}(X_t,\mc
  2286	L_t(n))$. Thus (\ref{eq:4b}) implies (\ref{eq:4c}).
  2287	
  2288	Finally, for any $t'\in T'$, any $i$, and any $n$,  we have
  2289		$$\uH^i\bigl(X_{t'},\mc L_{t'}(n)\bigr)
  2290		=\uH^i\bigl(X_{p(t')},\mc L_{p(t')}(n)\bigr)\ox_{k_t}k_{t'}$$
  2291	 because cohomology commutes with flat base change.  So  (\ref{eq:4c})
  2292	remains valid after the base change $p\:T'\to T$; whence, (\ref{eq:4b})
  2293	does too.  Thus the presheaf is well defined, and so $P^\phi_m$ is too. 
  2294	
  2295	Arguing much as we did for $P^\phi\x_PT$, we find, given a map $T\to
  2296	P^\phi$, that, as $m$ varies, the products $P^\phi_m\x_{P^\phi}T$ form a
  2297	nested sequence of open subschemes of $T$, whose union is $T$.  In the
  2298	argument, the key change is in proving openness.  In place of
  2299	\cite[7.9.11]{EGAIII2}, we use the following part of Serre's
  2300	Theorem~\cite[2.2.2]{EGAIII1}: given a coherent sheaf $\mc F$ on a
  2301	projective scheme over a Noetherian ring $A$, there are only finitely
  2302	many $i\ge1$ and $n\ge m$ such that $H^i(\mc F(n))$ is nonzero, and all
  2303	these nonzero $A$-modules are finitely generated.  Hence, if there is a
  2304	prime ${\bf p}$ of $A$ such that $H^i(\mc F(n))_{\bf p}=0$ for all
  2305	$i\ge1$ and $n\ge m$, then there is an $a\notin{\bf p}$ such that
  2306	$H^i(\mc F(n))_a=0$ for all $i\ge1$ and $n\ge m$.
  2307	
  2308	Therefore, again by \cite[(0, 4.5.4), p.~103]{EGAG}, it suffices to
  2309	represent each $P^\phi_m$ by a quasi-projective $S$-scheme.
  2310	
  2311	Fix $\phi$ and $m$.  Set $\phi_0(n):=\phi(m+n)$.  Then there is an
  2312	isomorphism of functors $P^\phi_m \risom P^{\phi_0}_0$, which is defined
  2313	as follows.  First, define an endomorphism $\varepsilon$ of $\Pic_{X/S}$
  2314	by sending an invertible sheaf $\mc L$ on an $X_T$ to $\mc L(m)$.
  2315	Plainly $\varepsilon$ is an automorphism.  So $\varepsilon$ induces an
  2316	automorphism $\varepsilon^+$ of the associated sheaf $P$.  Plainly
  2317	$\varepsilon^+$ carries $P^\phi_m$ onto $P^{\phi_0}_0$.  Thus it
  2318	suffices to represent $P^{\phi_0}_0$ by a quasi-projective $S$-scheme.

  2320	The function $s\mapsto\chi(X_s,\mc O_{\!X_s}(n))$ is locally constant on
  2321	$S$ by \cite[7.9.11]{EGAIII2}.  Hence we may assume it is constant by

  2323	O_{\!X_s}(n))$.

  2326	$\Div_{X/S}$ is a scheme, in fact, an open subscheme of the Hilbert

  2330	$\theta(n):=\psi(n)-\phi_0(n)$.  Plainly $Z$ lies in

  2368	\begin{lem}\label{lm:qt}
  2369	 Let $\alpha\:Z\to P$ be a map of \'etale sheaves, and set $R:=Z\x_PZ$.
  2370	Assume $\alpha$ is a surjection, $Z$ is representable by a
  2371	quasi-projective $S$-scheme, $R$ is representable by an $S$-scheme, and
  2372	the first projection $R\to Z$ is representable by a smooth and proper
  2373	map.  Then $P$ is representable by a quasi-projective $S$-scheme, and
  2374	$\alpha$ is representable by a smooth map.
  2375	 \end{lem}

  2377	\begin{proof} To lighten the notation, let $Z$ and $R$ denote the
  2378	corresponding schemes as well.  Since the structure map $Z\to S$ is
  2379	quasi-projective, it is separated; whence, the first projection
  2380	$Z\x_SZ\to Z$ is too.  But the first projection $R\to Z$ is proper, and
  2381	factors naturally through a map $h\:R\to Z\x_SZ$.  Hence $h$ is proper.
  2382	But $h$ is a monomorphism; that is, $h$ is injective on $T$-points.
  2383	Therefore, $h$ is a closed embedding by \cite[8.11.5]{EGAIV3}.
  2384	
  2385	Plainly, for each $S$-scheme $T$, the subset $R(T)\subset
  2386	Z(T)\x_{S(T)}Z(T)$ is the graph of an equivalence relation.  Also, the
  2387	map of schemes $R\to Z$ is flat and proper, and $Z$ is a
  2388	quasi-projective $S$-scheme.  It follows that there exist a
  2389	quasi-projective $S$-scheme $Q$ and a faithfully flat and projective map
  2390	$Z\to Q$ such that $R=Z\x_QZ$.  (In other words, a flat and proper
  2391	equivalence relation on a quasi-projective scheme is effective.)  In
  2392	fact, $R$ defines a map from $Z$ to the Hilbert scheme $\IHilb_{Z/S}$, and
  2393	its graph lies in the universal scheme as a closed subscheme, which
  2394	descends to $Q\subset \IHilb_{Z/S}$; for more details, see \cite[Thm.~(2.9),

  2398	smooth.  But these fibers are, up to extension of the ground field, the
  2399	same as those of $R\to Z$.  And $R\to Z$ is smooth by hypothesis.  Thus
  2400	$Z\to Q$ is smooth.

  2405	exist an \'etale covering $T'\to T$ and a $T$-map $T'\to A$ by
  2406	\cite[17.16.3 (ii)]{EGAIV4}.  Then $T'\to A\to Z$ is an element of
